Search cyclic two-plane orbit codes from scratch then break symmetry in stages with quenches and LP polish.
direction: Search a symmetry-constrained construction from scratch and then break the symmetry gradually: represent points as orbits under the two-plane rotation group generated by block-diagonal rotations through angles 2*pi/m and 2*pi*q/m in orthogonal coordinate planes of R^4, using orbit partitions summing to 153 such as three generic orbits of size 51 or nine generic orbits of size 17, optimise only the 3-9 seed points (with duplicate-orbit rejection) by annealed soft-max over the full 153-point Gram matrix for several coprime q values, then release the constraint in stages by adding per-point tangent noise of increasing scale 0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03 with a soft-max quench and LP polish at each stage. This produces balanced contact degrees and no rattler by construction, explores basins unreachable from the record, and should be run for about 60 seconds across q and partition choices before spending the remaining time on symmetry-broken polishing of the best orbit-derived seed.

idea: Overshoot to 154-156 via largest-hole insertion and prune back plus shrink to 142 and regrow to escape the 153 basin.
direction: Use continuation through neighbouring cardinalities to let the bottleneck reorganise under different pressure: starting from the record, build N=154, 155 and 156 codes by inserting each extra point at the largest spherical hole found from 50,000 random candidates (minimising its maximum cosine to existing points), jointly soft-max optimising and LP-polishing at each N, then return to 153 by trial-deleting candidates chosen from the inserted points and from high-contact-degree points, scoring each deletion by a short 1-second LP polish and keeping the best; also run the reverse path by deleting the rattler plus 10 random points to N=142, fully re-optimising there, and greedily regrowing to 153 by largest-hole insertion with a brief joint polish after each addition. Keep the best polished 153-point endpoint from all overshoot-and-prune and shrink-and-regrow trajectories, using graph-hash diversity to avoid repeating the record basin, and reserve 30 seconds for a final full LP polish.

idea: Break the isostatic jammed basin with Hopf-fiber symmetric restarts plus coherent cluster rigid-body kicks and worst-point hole relocations, each relaxed by hybrid long-range Riesz to short-range softmax annealing and tangent LP polishing.
Systematic one-edge contact-graph swaps forcing near-contacts to become active while banning an incident contact via constrained trust-region LPs, then unconstrained polishing.
direction: Force explicit contact-graph edge swaps using the near-contact pairs revealed by the slack gap: sort non-contact pairs by slack and take those ranked roughly 450-550 (slack about 1e-5 to 1e-3), then for each candidate pair (a,b) choose an existing contact edge (c,d) sharing a or b or incident to a degree-8 point, and run a constrained tangent LP/smoothing phase with trust radius 0.01-0.03 in which the linearised cosine of (a,b) is required to reach at least the current maximum minus 1e-7 while the linearised cosine of (c,d) is required to fall to at most the current maximum minus delta for delta in {1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3}, minimising t over all other near-maximal pairs. After 20-100 such constrained steps remove the artificial constraints, LP-polish the whole configuration, and accept the run for further polishing if the new pair remains within 1e-6 of the maximum and the banned pair has slack above 1e-6, thereby systematically enumerating at least 40 one-edge topology changes instead of hoping noise creates them.

idea: Force single-contact exchanges with constrained trust-region LP that opens one tied contact while closing an incident second-shell pair, then re-polish to a new basin.
Dual-weighted single-edge flips along the contact-Jacobian null mechanism to exchange one active contact for a near-active second-shell pair.
direction: Implement dual-guided single-edge flips by following a contact-Jacobian mechanism: compute the active contacts within $10^{-9}$, form their linearised Jacobian in the tangent spaces, and estimate nonnegative equilibrium/dual weights for the contacts using the final LP duals or nonnegative least squares; rank contacts by small weight, especially contacts incident to degree-3 or degree-4 vertices. For each of the best 20 weak contacts $e$ and each non-contact pair $f$ with slack below $2\times10^{-4}$ sharing a vertex with $e$, delete $e$, compute the smallest right-singular vector/mechanism of the remaining contact Jacobian after removing the six global rotations, orient it so the linearised cosine of $f$ decreases, and take projected line-search steps of sizes $0.001$–$0.03$ on $S^3$, rejecting steps that push any other cosine above the current maximum by more than the step tolerance. When $f$ reaches the active level or no further step is feasible, run the usual trust-region LP polish, record the sorted contact-degree hash, and retain the result only if it is a genuinely different hash or improves the score; spend at most about 120 seconds on these flips and always fall back to the best configuration found.

idea: Beam-search overshoot-and-prune with hole insertion, multi-criterion deletions and hash-diverse LP polishing.
direction: Use beam-search overshoot-and-prune instead of a single greedy overshoot chain: starting from the incumbent, greedily insert 12–17 additional points at approximate largest holes to obtain $N=165$–$170$, optimise the oversized code with annealed softmax and a short LP polish, and then prune back to 153 in stages while maintaining a beam of about 4–6 partial configurations. At each deletion stage, score candidate deletions by several different criteria—highest incident contact count, largest sum of near-maximal cosines, smallest loss of hole coverage, and random deletion—expand the beam using different criteria, apply short softmax/LP re-optimisation after every few deletions, and discard duplicate contact-degree hashes so the beam does not collapse to the record basin. After reaching 153, fully LP-polish every beam survivor, continue at least one branch that deletes a point which was present in the original record rather than only deleting inserted points, and return the best polished survivor if it beats the incumbent.

idea: Basin-hopping with hole-reinsertion, contact-guided subset kicks and global kicks screened by annealed softmax repulsion and short trust-region LP, keeping the best jam for a final long LP polish.
Frozen-exterior patch excision on low-degree vertices with maximin hole regrowth and masked annealing plus LP polish.
direction: Perform local patch excision and rebuilding rather than perturbing the whole sphere: choose patch centres among points with at most 4 contacts, remove the centre together with its contact neighbours and, if needed, its second neighbours to obtain patches of 6–10 deleted points, while freezing the remaining 143–147 points. For many random trials, place the deleted points by sequential maximin hole insertion against both frozen points and already reinserted points using at least $100{,}000$ random candidates on $S^3$, then optimise only the free patch points with the annealed softmax objective while including frozen points as fixed blockers, project gradients to tangent spaces, and finish with a full LP polish. Try patches centred on several distinct low-degree vertices and several random restarts per patch within the time budget, because the frozen exterior preserves most of the record while the patch interior is given enough freedom to acquire a completely new contact topology; keep candidates by exact maximum cosine and by contact-hash diversity, not merely by improvement over the patch objective.

idea: Overshoot-and-prune beam search from hole-augmented codes with load-based deletions and LP polishing.
direction: Redo overshoot-and-prune as a small, robust beam search that cannot crash the submission: start from the incumbent plus $6$, $9$, or $12$ hole-inserted points ($N=159,162,165$), briefly optimize the oversized code with a smooth minimax objective plus one short LP polish, then delete points one at a time, at each level keeping a beam of only 3 configurations scored by (max cosine, sum of near-contact loads within $10^{-4}$, diversity of degree hash), where the deletion criterion for a point is its total near-contact load $\sum_j \exp(-(m-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)/10^{-4})$ rather than max cosine alone. When $N$ reaches 153, LP-polish each beam leaf, deduplicate by sorted degree sequence and by configuration distance after orthogonal Procrustes alignment, and always return the best valid array found (initial incumbent if every branch fails); cap pair lists, wrap every LP in try/except, and hard-stop new branches at 160 s.

idea: Build 153-point codes as unions of Hurwitz-unit quaternion orbits with seed-only symmetric optimization then full annealed repulsion and LP polish.
direction: Search a structurally different basin from quaternion-orbit and 24-cell-type seeds instead of starting near the record: generate configurations as unions of orbits of 6–7 seed unit quaternions under left multiplication by the 24 Hurwitz units, giving 144–168 points before selecting or trimming to 153, optionally combined with randomly rotated copies of the standard 24-cell coordinates $(\pm1,\pm1,0,0)/\sqrt2$ and coordinate permutations. First optimise only the seed quaternions and a global rotation under the softmax objective so the initial configuration retains a regular, highly symmetric contact structure, then unfreeze all 153 points, run annealed softmax, and finish with LP polishing. Repeat with multiple random seeds, orbit choices, and partial-orbit fillings for the remaining points, selecting fillers by greedy maximin distance; this tests whether a more regular contact-degree and stress distribution can reach a better basin that local perturbations of the present irregular isostatic jam cannot reach.

idea: Melt-and-repack local patches and worst-point hole reinsertion with annealed softmax repulsion to force contact-graph changes, followed by trust-region LP re-jamming.

Escape the square jammed contact graph with deliberately multi-point nonlocal moves — rigid cap rotations, hole deletion/reinsertion, and smooth collective fields — each followed by annealed softmax repulsion and trust-region LP re-polish.
Overshoot with hole insertion then beam-search pruning by near-contact load with LP re-polish and safe fallbacks.
direction: Redo overshoot-and-prune as a small, robust beam search that cannot crash the submission: start from the incumbent plus $6$, $9$, or $12$ hole-inserted points ($N=159,162,165$), briefly optimize the oversized code with a smooth minimax objective plus one short LP polish, then delete points one at a time, at each level keeping a beam of only 3 configurations scored by (max cosine, sum of near-contact loads within $10^{-4}$, diversity of degree hash), where the deletion criterion for a point is its total near-contact load $\sum_j \exp(-(m-\langle x_i,x_j\rangle)/10^{-4})$ rather than max cosine alone. idea: Multi-contact cluster flips from NNLS stress weights with rotation-projected null mechanisms and short LP re-polish under a tabu hash.
direction: Perform simultaneous multi-contact cluster flips, not single-edge flips: compute the NNLS dual weights $w$ and rigidity Jacobian $J$ at the incumbent, grow connected clusters of 6--10 vertices by BFS from the lowest-$w$ contacts, delete $k\in\{4,6,8\}$ weak contacts in and around each cluster, project out the 6 global rotations, and take the smallest few right-singular vectors of the remaining $J$ as mechanisms. Line-search each mechanism over amplitudes $0.002$--$0.05$ (log-spaced, both signs), requiring at least two demoted contacts to reach slack $>10^{-5}$ while allowing a different near-contact to close, then LP-polish each candidate for 1--2 s with the usual trust-region LP, reject previously seen degree hashes (tol $5\times10^{-7}$), and keep a small tabu list; use $\le120$ s for flips and reserve the remainder for final polishing of the global best, with try/except fallback to the loaded best.

idea: Teleport low-degree points into genuine spherical holes with greedy LSE-refined reinsertion plus LP polish
direction: Teleport points instead of moving them locally: identify the degree-2 point and all degree $\le4$ points (or low incident dual weight), delete $r\in\{1,2,3,5\}$ of them, and reinsert each at a genuine hole of the remaining configuration by scoring $\ge30000$ random unit vectors plus jittered copies of removed points by their maximum cosine to the survivors, locally refining the best $\sim20$ holes by tangent descent on a smooth max ($\log$-sum-exp, $p\approx100$), inserting greedily one at a time. After each full reinsertion run LP polish, record the degree hash, and iterate with different deleted subsets/seeds until $\sim150$ s; this creates and destroys many contacts at once and tests whether a near-rattler should occupy a completely different spherical region rather than a neighbouring one.

idea: Multi-contact cluster flips from NNLS dual weights with projected Jacobian mechanisms and tabu LP re-polish.
direction: Perform simultaneous multi-contact cluster flips, not single-edge flips: compute the NNLS dual weights $w$ and rigidity Jacobian $J$ at the incumbent, grow connected clusters of 6--10 vertices by BFS from the lowest-$w$ contacts, delete $k\in\{4,6,8\}$ weak contacts in and around each cluster, project out the 6 global rotations, and take the smallest few right-singular vectors of the remaining $J$ as mechanisms. Line-search each mechanism over amplitudes $0.002$--$0.05$ (log-spaced, both signs), requiring at least two demoted contacts to reach slack $>10^{-5}$ while allowing a different near-contact to close, then LP-polish each candidate for 1--2 s with the usual trust-region LP, reject previously seen degree hashes (tol $5\times10^{-7}$), and keep a small tabu list; use $\le120$ s for flips and reserve the remainder for final polishing of the global best, with try/except fallback to the loaded best.

idea: Collective graph-cut twists moving 10-40 point blocks by random SO(4) rotations to force multi-contact topology changes, followed by smooth relaxation and LP re-polish.
Cluster-rigid basin hopping with multi-point delete-reinsert to escape the square jammed contact graph.
Teleport low-degree vertices to genuine spherical holes found by large random search plus jittered copies, refined by smooth-max tangent descent and greedily reinserted before LP polish.
direction: Teleport points instead of moving them locally: identify the degree-2 point and all degree $\le4$ points (or low incident dual weight), delete $r\in\{1,2,3,5\}$ of them, and reinsert each at a genuine hole of the remaining configuration by scoring $\ge30000$ random unit vectors plus jittered copies of removed points by their maximum cosine to the survivors, locally refining the best $\sim20$ holes by tangent descent on a smooth max ($\log$-sum-exp, $p\approx100$), inserting greedily one at a time. After each full reinsertion run LP polish, record the degree hash, and iterate with different deleted subsets/seeds until $\sim150$ s; this creates and destroys many contacts at once and tests whether a near-rattler should occupy a completely different spherical region rather than a neighbouring one.

idea: Multi-point basin hopping with hole deletion/reinsertion, cap rotations and collective kicks followed by annealed softmax repulsion and trust-region LP re-polish to escape the square jammed contact graph.
